operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names (Scientists, Projects, AssignedTo) and mixed-case columns (SSN, Name, Code, Hours, Scientist, Project) — must double-quote with original spelling.
Declared types mix case: 'INT', 'Char(30)', 'Char(4)', 'char(4)' — type dispatch must lower-case before matching.
Char(4) PK 'Code' holds 4-char alnum strings ('AeH1','Ast3','Bte1') — String fuzzer with length arg 4, not Number.
SSN is INT PK with 9-digit values (123234877) — Number fuzzer scale from 'int' (no args) => scale 0, range [-1,1] then perturbed; will not reproduce 9-digit magnitudes.
AssignedTo has composite PK (Scientist, Project) and two FKs to Scientists.SSN and Projects.Code — both parents exist and are unique PKs.
AssignedTo.Project distinct=8 < 12 rows: FK column has duplicate values (ties) — parent Code has 14 distinct, so FK draw with replacement is fine.
AssignedTo.Scientist distinct=12 = row count, but Scientists has 12 rows — FK coverage is full here; not guaranteed after PK dedup.
No NULLs anywhere (null_rate 0.0) despite SSN/Code/Hours being nullable — TS will still emit NULLs for nullable columns.
All storage classes match declared types (integer for INT, text for Char) — no affinity contradictions.
Tiny tables (12/14/12 rows) — choose_table_sizes will produce sizes 1..~2500, far larger than original; no huge-table sampling needed.
No views, triggers, indexes beyond PKs; DDL is plain CREATE TABLE — clone is trivial.
Projects.Hours distinct=13 of 14 (one duplicate) — Number fuzzer list-range quirk (upper end overwritten to full range) will widen values.
operator_ts_expectations: Scientists.SSN: Number fuzzer, scale 0, no args => range [-1,1], int perturb +-1/+-2; produces tiny/negative ints, never 9-digit — implausible SSNs (FN risk on SSN filters/joins).
Scientists.Name / Projects.Name: String fuzzer, length from Char arg (30/50), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contaminate — random gibberish names, not 'First Last' (FN on name LIKE/pattern queries).
Projects.Code: String length 4, random 4-char strings — will not match 'AeH1' style; queries filtering Code='AeH1' or LIKE 'Ae%' likely miss (FN).
Projects.Hours: Number scale 0, list range quirk => values near [-1,1] plus perturb, not 98..789 — range predicates (Hours>200) become trivially true/false (FN/FP).
AssignedTo.Scientist/Project: FK draw from parent final values with replacement — ties/duplicates expected, so join cardinalities differ from original (FP on COUNT/DISTINCT queries).
Composite PK (Scientist,Project) dedup keeps first occurrence — AssignedTo may shrink below requested size, reducing join fan-out (FP on aggregate queries).
Nullable SSN/Code/Hours will receive NULLs from String/Number samplers (p=0.2 fresh) — IS NULL / NOT NULL predicates flip (FP).
p=0.2 DB-level fuzz prob, 0.3 chance p=0 whole instance — some instances reuse only original 5 sampled values, others mostly fresh; variance drives both FN and FP.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) on non-PK columns limits fresh draws — small tables may repeat values, creating accidental ties (FP on DISTINCT/COUNT).
No CHECK constraints, no NOT NULL enforcement in Python — only PK/unique/NOT NULL at insert; NOT NULL Name columns will drop rows silently (rows_failed>0).
Date/Time/Bool fuzzers unused here (no such declared types) — all columns go to Number or String.
Self-FK absent; table order is Scientists, Projects -> AssignedTo (level 0 then level 1) — FK fill order is safe.
